主要内容: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that real gross domestic product (GDP) increased by 1.1 percent in the second quarter of 2016, according to the second estimate released on August 26, 2016. This growth rate was 0.1 percentage point less than the advance estimate from July. In the first quarter, real GDP rose by 0.8 percent. The increase in real GDP was primarily driven by higher consumer spending, particularly on nondurable goods like food and beverage items, durable goods such as recreational goods and vehicles, and services including housing, utilities, and healthcare. However, the growth was partially offset by a decline in inventory investment, with GDP less inventory investment (real final sales of domestic product) increasing by 2.4 percent. Other factors that partially offset GDP growth included declines in housing investment, state and local government spending, and business investment. The downward revision to the second estimate of GDP growth mainly reflected downward revisions to state and local government spending and inventory investment, as well as an upward revision to imports. Corporate profits decreased by 1.2 percent in the second quarter of 2016 after rising 3.4 percent in the first quarter.
